discussion_comments.comment_body:
> is this really needed?
> 
> since we already provide a check for this
> 
> ```ts
> const headerName = options?.headerName ?? 'X-Request-Id'
> ```


I haven't documented this yet, but it is for internal use only. For example, logging.
Specifying empty string means that the user expects no request ID to be present in  request/response.
And we need to check for empty string.

```ts
console.log("" ?? "string") // empty
console.log("" || "string") // string
console.log("" ? "A" : "B") // B
```

Due to this type declaration I have to write `const env = options!.env!` in `getPath` to get the bindings which feels a bit hacky/unnecessary. 

I tried changing this to:
```ts
readonly getPath: ((request: Request) => string) | ((request: Request, options: { env: E['Bindings'] }) => string)
```

So, basically some kind of overloading instead of an optional param. However, this didn't work out well:
- when declaring `getPath` as `getPath: (req) => { ... }` I get `Parameter 'req' implicitly has an 'any' type.` (i.e. this change would break backward compatibility)
- when declaring `getPath` as `getPath: (req, { env }) => { ... }` the `env` variable still has an optional type for whatever reason (i.e. `Bindings | undefined`)

I'm not super proficient in TypeScript, so I'm not exactly sure what's going on. Do you have any other idea on whether it'd be possible to make type declarations more user-friendly without introducing breaking changes?

I tried it, but `event.requestContext.http?.httpMethod` is `undefined`. So, `method` must be:

```ts
const method = 'httpMethod' in event ? event.httpMethod : event.requestContext.http.method
```

Without this, I'd have to add `as string | unknown` to line 79, which is ugly. Ideally we'd turn on [`"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig#noUncheckedIndexedAccess) in the tsconfig, but that makes _many_ things break so I consider it out of scope for this PR.
I think the previous code is fine. We just need to make the type for when it's undefined be `string | undefined` or `string | null`.
